claim: The Claude Agent SDK evaluates tool permission in a fixed precedence order (hooks, deny rules, ask rules, permission mode, allow rules, canUseTool callback) so that deny rules and PreToolUse hooks can block an action even under bypassPermissions mode.
stance_target: Concrete permission-scoping architecture exists today to constrain agent action at the infrastructure/SDK level
quoted_support: If a deny rule matches, the tool is blocked, even in bypassPermissions mode... Check ask rules from settings.json. If an ask rule matches, the call falls through to your canUseTool callback for confirmation, even in bypassPermissions mode.

claim: bypassPermissions mode auto-approves effectively every tool call except a narrow hard-coded carve-out, and the documentation explicitly warns 'Use with extreme caution. Claude has full system access in this mode. Only use in controlled environments where you trust all possible operations.'
stance_target: Fully permissive autonomous modes are safe as a default for scaled deployment
quoted_support: Use with extreme caution. Claude has full system access in this mode. Only use in controlled environments where you trust all possible operations.

claim: The SDK hard-codes a non-overridable protection: rm and rmdir removals targeting a 'critical path' are never auto-approved by any allow rule or even bypassPermissions mode, and must either reach a human callback or be denied outright depending on mode -- an explicit kill-switch carve-out baked into the permission engine itself.
stance_target: Concrete kill-switch/hard-stop design exists at the SDK level independent of configurable policy
quoted_support: rm and rmdir removals targeting a critical path are never approved by an allow rule... In bypassPermissions mode, Claude Code approves everything that reaches this step except rm and rmdir removals targeting a critical path, which fall through instead.

claim: Subagent permission inheritance is scoped: a subagent runs in bypassPermissions mode only when the parent session itself does, and an 'auto' permission mode value is applied to a subagent only when auto mode is available to that subagent -- constraining scope creep when an orchestrator (Director) spawns subagents (Workers).
stance_target: Permission scoping across Director/Worker delegation boundaries is an explicit, implementable design pattern today
scope_conditions: Claude Agent SDK subagent delegation, requires Claude Code v2.1.267+, 2026
quoted_support: A subagent runs in the parent session's permission mode unless you set permissionMode on its AgentDefinition... Even then, Claude Code never applies a "bypassPermissions" value, and applies an "auto" value only when auto mode is available to that subagent. A subagent runs in bypassPermissions mode only when the parent session itself does.

claim: The documentation warns that subagents may have different system prompts and less constrained behavior than the main agent, so inheriting bypassPermissions grants them full, autonomous system access -- a direct governance warning relevant to Director-spawned Worker fleets.
stance_target: Subagent/worker delegation is inherently safe without explicit permission-mode configuration
quoted_support: Subagents may have different system prompts and less constrained behavior than your main agent, so inheriting bypassPermissions grants them full, autonomous system access.

claim: A 'dontAsk' mode exists that converts any would-be permission prompt into a hard denial without ever invoking a human callback, offering a fully deterministic fail-closed governance posture for headless/high-concurrency agent deployment.
stance_target: Concrete fail-closed (deny-by-default) governance control is implementable today for headless/scaled agents
quoted_support: dontAsk: Deny instead of prompting. Any call that would otherwise prompt is denied... canUseTool is never called.
